subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction and memoryFlush from the foreground session lane, or keep the current foreground lane model with shorter timeouts and diagnostic recovery?
rationale: The bug is source-backed, but the durable fix changes scheduler and session-state ordering guarantees for interactive turns versus context maintenance.

options.title: Isolate compaction lane
options.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency lane or worker so foreground user messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for maintenance to finish.

options.title: Preempt foreground maintenance
options.body: Keep the current lane model but make compaction and memoryFlush abortable and reschedulable when foreground messages arrive.

options.title: Accept mitigation only
options.body: Treat the 180-second compaction timeout and stuck-session recovery as sufficient, accepting that foreground turns can still queue during active maintenance.

recommendation.title: Isolate compaction lane
recommendation.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency lane or worker so foreground user messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for maintenance to finish.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest concrete history points to recent preflight compaction and queued compaction work in the affected files.
